mechanism_narrative: Persistent weakness in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES signals fewer commuting and downtown trips, which suppresses discretionary retail visits and keeps RETAIL_REC lower over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If TRANSIT and WORKPLACES stay near current levels but RETAIL_REC rises above its last-4-week mean over the next 28 days, the mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL remains elevated while TRANSIT and WORKPLACES stay depressed, households substitute toward local spending and home-centered routines, which reduces retail-and-recreation mobility within four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL stays above +8 while TRANSIT remains below -35 for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL stays above +8 and TRANSIT stays below -35 for two weeks yet RETAIL_REC does not fall within the following 14 days, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in PARKS mobility reflects more outdoor leisure trips and broader relaxation of movement constraints, which spills into higher retail-and-recreation visits over the next one to two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises by at least 10 points week-on-week after being below -15
failure_condition: If PARKS rises by 10 points or more from a depressed level but RETAIL_REC does not increase within 7 days, reject the mechanism.

mechanism_narrative: A renewed fall in TRANSIT below its already weak baseline indicates tighter movement controls or stronger avoidance behavior, and that shock reduces RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -40 and remains there for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: If TRANSIT remains below -40 for two weeks but RETAIL_REC is flat or higher over the next 28 days, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When GROCERY_PHARM stays only mildly negative while RESIDENTIAL is elevated, consumers consolidate trips and avoid discretionary shopping, causing RETAIL_REC to drift lower over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM remains near current levels and RESIDENTIAL stays elevated but RETAIL_REC rises within 14 days, this mechanism fails.

mechanism_narrative: A broad late-winter improvement in parks and transit activity marks a seasonal normalization of outings and errands, which should lift retail-and-recreation mobility over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS and TRANSIT both improve by at least 8 points from their recent four-week lows
evidence_refs: fact:weekly means are observed through mid-August 2020
failure_condition: If PARKS and TRANSIT both recover from recent lows but RETAIL_REC does not exceed its last-4-week mean by the end of four weeks, reject the hypothesis.

mechanism_narrative: A further deterioration in WORKPLACES below its current level signals renewed suppression of nonessential trips, and that translates into lower retail-and-recreation mobility within one week.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES falls below -17 after already being below -15
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES drops below -17 and RETAIL_REC does not decline within 7 days, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT stops worsening while GROCERY_PHARM and WORKPLACES remain depressed, retail mobility stabilizes first and then rises because essential-trip patterns resume before leisure shopping does.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT improves by at least 3 points week-on-week while GROCERY_PHARM stays below -4 and WORKPLACES stays below -15
failure_condition: If TRANSIT improves while GROCERY_PHARM and WORKPLACES remain depressed but RETAIL_REC does not rise within 14 days, the mechanism fails.
